353008.title: Caporossi–Dobrynin–Gutman–Hansen conjecture on odd-diameter H-palindromic trees
353008.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of diameter $D$, and write $\alpha(G,k)$ for the number of unordered pairs of vertices at distance $k$. The graph is **H-palindromic** when

$$
\alpha(G,k)=\alpha(G,D-k)
$$

for every $k=0,1,\dots,\left\lfloor{\frac{D}{2}}\right\rfloor$. In particular, let $T$ be a tree of odd diameter. **Caporossi–Dobrynin–Gutman–Hansen conjecture.** There are no H-palindromic trees of odd diameter. This conjecture would rule out the existence of any tree satisfying the coefficient symmetry for odd diameter; the source also records that exactly five H-palindromic trees of even diameter were known from earlier work.

354762.title: Cycle obstruction conjecture for ground-graph-independent blowup Ramsey numbers
354762.statement:
Let $r\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $H$ be a graph containing a cycle. Write $G\stackrel{r}{\to}H$ when every $r$-colouring of the edges of $G$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$, and let $H[t]$ denote the $t$-blowup of $H$.

**Cycle obstruction conjecture.** There exists an integer $t$ such that, for every $s$, there is a graph $G$ satisfying

$$
G\stackrel{r}{\to}H\quad\text{but}\quad G[s]\not\stackrel{r}{\to}H[t].
$$

Together with the proved ground-graph-independent behaviour for forests, this conjecture would classify forests as exactly the finite graphs whose blowup Ramsey numbers do not depend on the ground graph. The source establishes the required obstruction for 3-chromatically connected graphs, while the assertion for every graph containing a cycle remains open.

356555.title: Manvel's Kelly conjecture on large-graph \ell-reconstructibility
356555.statement: For a graph $G$, its $k$-deck is the multiset of induced subgraphs with $k$ vertices, and $G$ is **$\ell$-reconstructible** when it is determined by the deck obtained by deleting $\ell$ vertices. **Manvel's Kelly conjecture.** For each natural number $\ell$, there is a threshold $M_\ell$ such that every graph with at least $M_\ell$ vertices is $\ell$-reconstructible. This generalizes Ulam's reconstruction conjecture to deletion of an arbitrary fixed number of vertices; the paper presents it as a conjecture and the supplied text gives no resolution.

360349.title: The bounded connectivity conjecture for breadth-critical tangles
360349.statement: Let $k\geq 2$ and let $M$ be a matroid with a breadth-critical tangle $\mathcal{T}$ of order at least $k$. A matroid is **$(s_0,s_1,\ldots,s_t)$-connected** if, whenever $F\subseteq E(M)$ has $\lambda(F)=i$ for $i\in\{0,1,\ldots,t\}$, either $|F|\leq s_i$ or $|E(M)-F|\leq s_i$. **The bounded connectivity conjecture.** There is an infinite sequence $(s_0,s_1,s_2,\ldots)$ such that, for all $k\geq 2$, if $\mathcal{T}$ is a breadth-critical tangle of order at least $k$ in $M$, then $M$ is $(s_0,s_1,\ldots,s_{k-2})$-connected. This would extend the established fact that breadth-critical tangles of order at least $4$ occur in weakly $4$-connected, equivalently $(0,1,4)$-connected, matroids; the existence of a uniform sequence for all orders remains open.

361033.title: Existence of nut graphs with two vertex orbits and three edge orbits
361033.statement:
Let $n\geq 9$ be a composite integer. A **nut graph** is a graph whose adjacency matrix has nullity one and whose nullspace is spanned by a vector with no zero entries; write $o_v(G)$ and $o_e(G)$ for the numbers of vertex and edge orbits of $G$, respectively. The preceding theorem establishes existence with $o_v(G)=2$ for every such $n$. **Existence conjecture.** For every $n\geq 9$ that is not prime, there exists a nut graph $G$ of order $n$ with

$$
o_v(G)=2\qquad\text{and}\qquad o_e(G)=3.
$$

The conjecture strengthens the established two-vertex-orbit existence result by requiring exactly three edge orbits; the source gives no resolution beyond describing this as a belief about the corresponding table row.

361975.title: Sintiari–Trotignon conjecture on treewidth of diamond-free even-hole-free graphs
361975.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $\operatorname{tw}(G)$ denote its treewidth. A graph is **even-hole-free** if it has no induced cycle of even length at least four, and the **diamond** is the graph on four vertices with five edges. **Sintiari–Trotignon's conjecture.** For every integer $t\geq 1$, there exists a constant $c_t$ such that every even-hole-free graph $G$ with no induced diamond and no clique of size $t$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{tw}(G)\leq c_t.
$$

This conjecture was resolved in the cited work TWXI, so the asserted bounded-treewidth conclusion is now a theorem.

362163.title: Botler, Colucci and Kohayakawa's additive bound conjecture for the mod $k$ chromatic index
362163.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph and let $k\geq 2$ be an integer. A $\chi'_{k}$-coloring of $G$ is an edge coloring such that the subgraph induced by the edges of each color has all degrees congruent to $1\pmod{k}$; write $\chi'_{k}(G)$ for the minimum number of colors in such a coloring. **Botler, Colucci and Kohayakawa's conjecture.** There is a constant $C$ such that

$$
\chi'_{k}(G)\leq k+C
$$

for every graph $G$. This conjecture asks whether the linear bound can always have additive constant independent of $k$; the paper improves the previously known bound from $198k-101$ to $177k-93$, but does not resolve the conjecture.

362516.title: The traceability conjecture for k-traceable oriented graphs
362516.statement:
A digraph $D$ is **$k$-traceable** if its order is at least $k$ and each of its induced subdigraphs of order $k$ is traceable; an oriented graph is a digraph obtained by orienting the edges of an undirected graph, and a digraph is **traceable** if it contains a hamiltonian directed path.

**Traceability conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 2$, every $k$-traceable oriented graph of order at least $2k-1$ is traceable.

This conjecture extends Rédei's theorem that every tournament is traceable and strengthens results for strongly connected digraphs with independence number two. Its resolution status is not established by the supplied source material.

367371.title: Robust Hajnal–Szemerédi conjecture for induced $K_r$-factors
367371.statement:
Let $r\geq 2$, let $n$ be divisible by $r$, and let $G$ be an $(\tfrac{(r-1)n}{r}+1)$-regular graph on $n$ vertices. A subset of $V(G)$ **induces a $K_r$-factor** if its induced subgraph has a partition into vertex-disjoint copies of $K_r$. **Robust Hajnal–Szemerédi conjecture.** For every $r\geq 2$, there is an $\varepsilon>0$ such that at least

$$
\varepsilon 2^n
$$

subsets of $V(G)$ induce a $K_r$-factor.

This is a robust analogue of the Hajnal–Szemerédi theorem, replacing the existence of one $K_r$-factor by a positive proportion of subsets inducing one. The supplied source gives no resolution status.

369933.title: BFP conjecture on nut graphs with two vertex and three edge orbits
369933.statement: Let $n$ be the order of a graph, and let a **nut graph** be a graph whose adjacency matrix is singular with one-dimensional null space spanned by an eigenvector having no zero entries. Vertex and edge orbits are the orbits of the automorphism group on the vertex set and edge set, respectively. **BFP's conjecture.** For every non-prime integer $n\geq 9$, there exists a nut graph $\Gamma$ of order $n$ with two vertex orbits and three edge orbits. The conjecture refines the known existence of nut graphs with two vertex orbits for every non-prime order $n\geq 9$ by requiring exactly three edge orbits.

370719.title: General chromatic cut conjecture
370719.statement:
Let $k$ be an integer, let $G$ be a graph with at least $k$ vertices, and let $X$ be one side of a cut of $G$. Write $V(G)$ and $E(G)$ for the vertex and edge sets, and let $\chi(G[X])$ denote the chromatic number of the subgraph induced by $X$. **General chromatic cut conjecture.** For every integer $k$ and every graph $G$ on at least $k$ vertices, if

$$
|E(G)| < k|V(G)| - \frac{k(k+1)}{2},
$$

then $G$ admits a cut $X$ with $\chi(G[X])<k$. In particular, $\ell_k=k$. This conjecture generalizes the small cases, including the bipartite-cut assertion for $k=3$, and remains open; the paper records only partial bounds for forest and bipartite cuts.

371207.title: Day–Johnson nonexistence conjecture for equilibria in hypercube Voronoi games
371207.statement: Let $Q_n$ be the discrete $n$-dimensional hypercube, and let a $k$-player profile be a tuple of $k$ chosen vertices of $Q_n$. A profile is **in equilibrium** if no player can strictly increase their score by moving to a different vertex. **Day–Johnson's conjecture.** For any fixed $k\geq 5$, there exists some $N$ such that, for any $n\geq N$, there are no $k$-player profiles in equilibrium on $Q_n$. The conjecture asserts eventual nonexistence of equilibria for every fixed number of at least five players; it remains open for all $k\geq 5$.

371858.title: Existence conjecture for non-trivial $F$-irregular graphs
371858.statement:
Let $F$ be a connected graph of order at least $3$. An **$F$-irregular graph** is a graph in which no two distinct vertices have isomorphic $F$-neighbourhoods.

**Existence conjecture.** For every connected graph $F$ of order $3$ or more, there exists a non-trivial $F$-irregular graph.

The conjecture concerns the existence of irregular graphs relative to an arbitrary connected graph $F$. It is known for stars and complete graphs of order at least $3$, but the general case is not resolved in the supplied text.

372143.title: Füredi's linear connected-matching conjecture
372143.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. A **connected matching** is a matching $M\subseteq E(G)$ such that for every two edges $e,f\in M$, an endpoint of $e$ is adjacent to an endpoint of $f$. **Füredi's linear connected-matching conjecture.** There is a constant $c>0$ such that every graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)=2$ has a connected matching of size at least 
$$
c|V(G)|.
$$
 The paper states that this conjecture is equivalent to the epsilon conjecture and attributes it to Füredi; a proof of the equivalence is known.

372150.title: The Induced Menger Conjecture
372150.statement: Let $G$ be a graph and let $X,Y\subseteq V(G)$. An **$(X,Y)$-path** is a path with one endpoint in $X$ and the other in $Y$, and two paths are **anti-complete** if they are vertex-disjoint and no edge of $G$ has one endpoint in each path. Write $N_G[Z]$ for the closed neighbourhood of $Z$. **The Induced Menger Conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, every graph $G$ and $X,Y\subseteq V(G)$ satisfies one of the following: $G$ contains $k$ pairwise anti-complete $(X,Y)$-paths; or there exists a set $Z\subseteq V(G)$ with $|Z|\leqslant k-1$ such that $G-N_G[Z]$ has no $(X,Y)$-path. This is the induced analogue of Menger's theorem and corresponds to the $d=2$ case of the coarse Menger conjecture; the paper's induced $\mathcal{A}$-path theorem provides evidence but does not resolve it.

372153.title: Composite-flow coverage conjecture for elementary abelian 2-groups
372153.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\mathcal{F}(G,\mathbb{Z}_2^k)$ denote the reconfiguration graph of nowhere-zero $\mathbb{Z}_2^k$-flows. A nowhere-zero $\mathbb{Z}_2^k$-flow $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$ is **composite** if there is a partition $A,B$ of $\{1,\ldots,k\}$ such that, for every edge $e\in E(G)$, there are $i\in A$ and $j\in B$ for which $e$ is in the support of both $f_i$ and $f_j$. **The composite-flow coverage conjecture.** There is an integer $k\geq 9$ such that, for any 2-edge-connected graph $G$, every connected component of $\mathcal{F}(G,\mathbb{Z}_2^k)$ contains a composite flow. The conjecture proposes that composite flows occur in every reconfiguration component, but its status remains open.

372328.title: Toroczkai's existence conjecture for prime gap graphs
372328.statement:
Let $p_n$ be the $n$-th prime, with $p_0=1$, and let

$$
\mathrm{PD}_n=\left(p_{\ell}-p_{\ell-1}\right)_{\ell=1}^{n}
$$

be the first $n$ prime gap sequence. A **prime gap graph** on $n\geq 2$ vertices is a simple graph whose vertex degrees are exactly the entries of $\mathrm{PD}_n$. **Toroczkai's existence conjecture.** For every $n\geq 2$, there exists a prime gap graph on $n$ vertices.

The conjecture asserts graphicality of every finite initial segment of the prime gap sequence; the paper establishes explicit unconditional graphicality only beyond a very large threshold, so the full assertion remains open.

372773.title: Coarse Gallai conjecture for A-paths
372773.statement: Let $G$ be a graph and let $A$ be a subset of the vertices of $G$. An **$A$-path** is a path in $G$ whose two endpoints belong to $A$. For subsets $X$ of vertices of $G$ and integers $r\geq 0$, let $B_G(X,r)$ denote the set of vertices at distance at most $r$ from $X$. Two subgraphs are at distance at least $d$ if the distance between their vertex sets is at least $d$. **Coarse Gallai conjecture.** There exist functions $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and $g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ such that for all positive integers $k$ and $d$, for every graph $G$ and every subset $A$ of the vertices of $G$, either $G$ contains $k$ $A$-paths which are pairwise at distance at least $d$, or there exists a set $X$ of the vertices of $G$ with $|X|\leq f(k)$ such that every $A$-path in $G$ contains a vertex of $B_G(X,g(d))$. This strengthens the coarse Erdős–Pósa-type statement by requiring the radius of the hitting balls to depend only on $d$, while the size of the hitting set depends only on $k$.

375993.title: Chartrand–Holbert–Oellermann–Swart conjecture on F-irregular graphs
375993.statement:
Let $F$ be a connected graph of order at least $3$. A graph $G$ is **$F$-irregular** if every vertex of $G$ has a distinct number of subgraphs isomorphic to $F$ that contain it. A graph is nontrivial if it has at least one edge.

**Chartrand–Holbert–Oellermann–Swart conjecture.** For every connected graph $F$ of order at least $3$, there exists a nontrivial $F$-irregular graph.

The conjecture generalizes the distinction of vertices by ordinary degree, corresponding to $F=K_2$, for which no nontrivial graph is $F$-irregular. It is known for several classes, including stars, complete graphs, and paths, but is not stated as fully resolved here.

376120.title: Weak Jackson–Thomassen orientation conjecture
376120.statement: A digraph $D$ is **$k$-strong** if it has at least $k+1$ vertices and remains strongly connected after the deletion of any set of at most $k-1$ vertices. An **orientation** of a digraph is an oriented spanning subdigraph obtained by deleting precisely one arc from every directed 2-cycle. **Weak Jackson–Thomassen conjecture.** There exists a function $f(k)$ so that every $f(k)$-strong digraph on at least $2k+1$ vertices contains a spanning $k$-strong oriented graph. This natural weakening is open for general digraphs already when $k=2$, although it holds for symmetric digraphs for all $k$.
